title: notification-01: Model + Config
summary: Tipi core del dominio notifiche, adapter verso ToastSpec, e schema config notification_system.
description: NotificationSource, NotificationSeverity (+ EnumArg/FromStr per l'azione notify), NotificationLifecycle, AppNotification, NotificationAction (Vec, keyed dal nome del proprio intent), NotificationDraft builder, project_visible_toast/to_toast_spec verso ToastSpec::action(key,label)/ToastPosition.
notes:
**Handoff context update:**
Domain model + the full raising-API redesign are the bulk of this phase's current work. T188/T189/T190/T192/T193/T184/T185 (core model) are done and verified by cargo check + tests. T493 (the public Notification builder, replacing pass 1's state.notifications.push shape entirely) is the current, unfinished task — see the phase handoff for the settled API, what's built, and what's explicitly not.

**Remaining work:**
T493: pane-creation producer, a test proving Notification::send() is the only public raise door, re-run the full lint-changed.sh gates after this session's changes, then the closure action form as its own piece of work. T186/T191 (config schema) remain untouched. Nothing in this phase has been visually verified by Antonio.

---
**Handoff context update:**
Core model + store + dispatch + mount done (P055/T491, P056 all, P059 all, P060 mount/bridge/state, P061 core model). This session: T493 (public Notification builder + single raise door notification::raise + pane-creation producer with a Focus action + tests) code-complete and green; auto_dismiss_ms config ([settings.notification_system], T186/T187/T191 in effect) done; both lint gates exit 0. None driven by Antonio.

**Remaining work:**
T493 drive-through + Antonio's call on pane-id-vs-name. T503 (wire or delete the per-severity lifetime). T191's history_limit knob (hardcoded 50). Closure action form (deferred). Formal closure of T186/T187/T191. Then P057 (tests/README), P062 (reload producer), P055's other producers. The toast pointer bug is NOT this phase — it is P097 (One Tree).
goals: Definire AppNotification/NotificationDraft/NotificationAction come modello app-owned, text-only, mai con Component/ViewNode, e l'adapter che li proietta su ToastSpec/ToastAction del widget grid-ui.
nonGoals: Contenuto ricco (ViewNode body/actions): deliberatamente fuori scope, il modello resta text-only anche dopo che il percorso ricco esistera altrove (host-side builder sullo ToastStack, non un campo qui).
Config schema completo di [settings].notification_system (T186/T191): oggi un placeholder hardcoded.
dependencies: heca-grid-ui ToastSpec/ToastAction/ToastPosition (T486-488 su origin/feat/hint-anything-actionable, gia atterrati).
risks: Nessuno noto: il gap di crate-graph (ToastSpec non puo contenere un ViewNode) e stato chiuso spostando il contenuto ricco a un builder host-side, non a un campo sul modello.
decisions: Notification::send() is the only public raise door; NotificationRuntime::push AND NotificationStore::push are pub(crate); notification::raise is the single Instant::now() site.
The pane-creation producer identifies the pane by id, not name (pane_name() is empty by design). Antonio to decide program-name / per-workspace-number.
auto_dismiss_ms at [settings.notification_system], default 4000ms, applied at the NotificationRuntime boundary to any Auto(_) lifetime; Sticky/explicit untouched; re-applied on reload.
default_lifetime_for_severity is designed but unwired — every notification auto-dismisses today including errors; T503 owns the wire-or-delete decision.
The toast pointer bug is an input-architecture problem, split to P097(F009) with docs/input-architecture.md as the contract; rejected a second dispatcher and a host-maintained surface list.

tasks.title: Public Notification builder API — redesign the raise path
tasks.description:
Antonio ruled (mid-session, after pass 1 shipped) that the raise API built for pass 1 — `state.notifications.push(NotificationDraft::info(..), Instant::now())` — is wrong as public API: it exposes a host-private field, a manually-supplied clock, and the store's internal verb ("push") to every producer and future plugin author. Full redesign required, settled with heca-4b across several messages.

FINAL SPEC:
```rust
Notification::info("Build finished")
    .body("3 warnings in heca-grid-ui")
    .action(NotificationAction::new("View log", Intent::new("open_pane_log").arg("pane_id", PropValue::Int(id)))
        .variant(ButtonVariant::Ghost))
    .send();
```

- `Notification` is a NEW public type (heca/src/notification.rs), public API from line one — a plugin author and a native producer type the identical line. `.info/.success/.warning/.danger(title)`, `.body(..)`, `.dedup_key(..)`, `.action(NotificationAction)` (chainable, ordered — matches `actions: Vec<..>`), terminal `.send()`.
- `.send()` has NO timestamp/delay argument at all (`.now()`/`.at()` were both rejected in discussion) — absent means deliver now; the store stamps the time itself, host-side, when the notification is actually accepted.
- `NotificationAction` gains a `variant: ButtonVariant` field (default `Primary`), mirroring `ToastAction`'s exact spelling (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/toast/spec.rs`) — label, intent, variant is the field order. `to_toast_spec`/`project_visible_toast` must map to `.action_with(ToastAction::new(key, label).variant(variant))` instead of the plain `.action(key,label)` sugar.
- `.send()` reaches the store via a HOST-INSTALLED SINK, not a threaded-in emitter or a global mutable store — same house pattern as `heca-grid-ui`'s `install_frame_request`/`request_frame()` (thread-local, installed once at startup). Concretely: a new `AppEvent::RaiseNotification { draft: NotificationDraft }` variant; `.send()` posts it through the installed sink (`event_proxy.send_event`); `main.rs`'s `user_event` handles it by calling `state.notifications.push(draft, Instant::now())` — the ONE place `Instant::now()` is read, by the host, not the caller.
- `NotificationStore::push`/`NotificationRuntime::push` (the deterministic `(draft, now)` primitive tests still want) must become `pub(crate)` at most — NOT re-exported as public API. The only public raise door is `Notification::...send()`. Add a test asserting this (the public surface has no other way to raise one).
- First consumer: pane creation raises `Notification::info(format!("Pane {name} created")).send()` — write it against the new API, not the old `push`.

DEFERRED, NOT this task — needs its own careful design, do not rush a partial version: the CLOSURE action form (`.action(label, variant, || { .. })`, registering an anonymous name-keyed action on the fly). Settled constraints for whoever builds it: (1) it must NOT appear in the command palette; (2) register/unregister must happen on the SAME boundary — register only once the notification is actually *accepted into* the store (so a deduped or over-cap-queued-then-expired notification never registers a leaked handler), unregister when it leaves the store by any path (dismiss/expire/history-evict), tested by raising the same dedup key twice and asserting the registry doesn't grow. A queued (not yet visible) notification still exists in the store and must follow the same register/unregister boundary as a visible one.

No priority/importance field on notifications — confirmed explicitly not wanted; severity is tone, not importance.

tasks.title: Wire the per-severity notification lifetime into the draft builder
tasks.description:
GOAL: make default_lifetime_for_severity (heca/src/notification.rs) actually take effect. It is designed — Error/Warning → Sticky, Success/Info → auto-dismiss — but has ZERO production callers; it is referenced only by tests. Its doc was corrected 2026-08-27 to say so plainly.

CURRENT STATE:
- NotificationDraft::new sets lifecycle: NotificationLifecycle::default() = Auto(5s). NotificationDraft::info/success/warning/danger only set severity, never lifecycle. AppNotification::new also defaults to Auto(5s).
- Result: TODAY EVERY NOTIFICATION AUTO-DISMISSES, including errors and warnings.
- The configured auto-dismiss duration ([settings.notification_system] auto_dismiss_ms, default 4000) is applied at the runtime boundary in NotificationRuntime::push via NotificationLifecycle::with_auto_duration — it rewrites any Auto(_) to Auto(configured) and leaves Sticky alone. So the config knob works; it just governs every notification because nothing is Sticky by default yet.

WORK:
- Decide the model: does a producer that calls Notification::warning("...") get a Sticky notification automatically (per default_lifetime_for_severity), or does the producer opt in with .sticky()? Antonio's stance so far: keep it simple, config governs auto-dismiss timing, severity is tone not importance, no priority field. So the likely answer is Info/Success/Warning/Error ALL auto-dismiss at auto_dismiss_ms unless the producer says .sticky() — which is current behaviour and means default_lifetime_for_severity should be DELETED, not wired.
- If instead per-severity stickiness is wanted: apply default_lifetime_for_severity in the draft's severity setters (or resolve it at push time from severity), and reconcile with auto_dismiss_ms (the config value fills the Auto arms; Sticky arms ignore it).
- Update the tests that reference default_lifetime_for_severity either way.
- This is a small decision-then-execute task; the decision is Antonio's.

Relates to T190 (severity + ToastSeverity mapping, done) and T191 (NotificationSystem config enum, planned).

---
**Completion summary:**
RESOLVED by DELETION, per Antonio's settled stance (severity is tone not importance; no priority field; keep it simple; config governs auto-dismiss).

- `default_lifetime_for_severity` (heca/src/notification.rs) removed. It was designed (Error/Warning → Sticky, Success/Info → Auto) but had zero production callers — the draft builder never applied it.
- New rule, stated in a comment where the function was: notifications do NOT vary lifetime by severity. Every notification auto-dismisses after `[settings.notification_system] auto_dismiss_ms`; a producer that needs one to persist opts in with `NotificationDraft::sticky()`.
- `NotificationLifetime::default()` doc updated: the duration is a placeholder the runtime rewrites to `auto_dismiss_ms`.
- Test `default_lifetime_for_severity_maps_each_variant` replaced with `severity_does_not_change_the_default_lifetime` (builds a draft at each severity, asserts identical default lifecycle).

CONSEQUENCE Antonio should know when he drives it: an ERROR toast also auto-dismisses after auto_dismiss_ms now. If he wants errors to persist by default, the reversal is small — re-add the mapping and apply it in the draft's severity setters. Flagged in the P061 handoff.

VERIFICATION: ./scripts/lint-changed.sh test exit 0 (notification 63/63); ./scripts/lint-changed.sh exit 0, heca clippy-clean. Not driven by Antonio.
FILES: heca/src/notification.rs.
DECISION: severity does not change lifetime; sticky is opt-in per notification.
